items.title: pushOrigin: one process that sends commits already made when the clone is behind origin, for Andy (from Jobs) and publishData
items.box:
PUSHORIGIN: SEND COMMITS ALREADY MADE TO GITHUB, EVEN WHEN THE CLONE IS BEHIND

WHAT IT DOES
- Lives in spirit/run/process/js/pushOrigin/pushOrigin.js (Andy's stub, 1818d97f).
- Fetches origin, re-stacks the checkout's own commits on its newest (unsaved edits put aside and back), pushes, and tries again if someone pushed meanwhile.
- On a clash (both sides changed the same lines) it stops, leaves the checkout as it was, and says why.

WHO STARTS IT
- publishData, in place of its own pull --rebase: it loads pushOrigin.js as shared code. Its commits keep passing commitCheck (its own folder only).
- Andy, by hand, from the Jobs launcher: pushOrigin.json lists its arguments the way wordpressScanner.json does, the launcher draws the dialog (index.html 1472-1562) and hands them over as one JSON string (wordpressScanner.js 85 reads them the same way). The node must list process/js/pushOrigin/, or jobs.create refuses it (jobs.js 404-418).
- Not goalShare: it keeps its own way, one new commit of currentGoal.json (goalShare.js 52-74).
- Not Andy's day-to-day commits: those go through VS Code's Sync Changes ("git.rebaseWhenSync": true).

ANDY, VERBATIM
- "I run into the problem that you ran into while pushing measurements. happens often to me, that's why i want a unified approach that i can trigger from desk, separately from goalShare, so we want one unified shared approach, that ensures my commits go through."
- To how Desk starts it: "Implicitly, by design, or via jobs-selector manually"
- "correct", and "it  must live in: spirit/run/process/js/pushOrigin/pushOrigin.js"
- "i only plan commits in folders outside of the actual code. if vscode gives me an easy ui-options to sync and push, i'll use that."
- "agreed. so it' just about sharing code among desk components."
- "jobs provides argument introspection and create a dialog for arguments automatically", "the process interface that is", "the launcher in shell builds an input dialog automatically"
- "look at spirit\run\process\js\wordpressScanner\wordpressScanner.js"
- andy/NOFACE.md: "during the creation of spirit/run/process/js/deskClient/publishData.js, when that script was run simultaneously on three platforms, by three instances of claude, conflicts arose when trying to push new measurment documents to github." / "A fix was applied to publishData.js that fixed the problem automatically" / "That fix would be extremely useful for deskServer as well. I propose to isolate that fixed section and make it available as spirit/run/process/js/deskClient/publishData.js so desk can use it when updating in goalShare.js, which mabe already carries the fix (duplicated) as well."
- The stub: "This is where we put the SpiritOS process for pushing changes to github when out commit livel is behind the remote origin."

WHY NOT GOALSHARE'S WAY FOR publishData
- It builds commits with commit-tree, which runs no commit-msg hook, so commitCheck would not see them (claude-windows's find; wsl-claude's conclusion).

OPEN: his Go.

In plain words: there are two kinds of push.
- A tool's push: "put these files on GitHub". Desk makes a new commit of them on GitHub's newest and pushes; your folder is untouched. goalShare does that today.

items.title: fileServer: slots the node reserves for itself (PROFILE_PICTURE)
items.box:
FILESERVER: SLOTS THE NODE RESERVES FOR ITSELF (PROFILE_PICTURE)

SHAPE
- A slot is a fixed label, listed once in fileServer (RESERVED = ['PROFILE_PICTURE']).
- Protected: push refuses a file named like a slot; pushing a slot's own bytes under another name answers the hash and leaves the slot's label where it is.
- Filled by one new owner-only verb, fill {slot, path}: the new file takes the label, the old file is deleted, and grants on the old file move to the new one: fill serves the new file's verb first (else unknown-path, apiAuth.js 90), then jobs.authSearch, jobs.authGrant and jobs.authRevoke on the loopback (server.js 1832-1836; wsl-claude). No new auth verb.
- Read by peers with what is there: every held file is a verb in the node's api list (fileServer.js 331-334), its info answers its one label (fileServer.js 84); the api list is subject to grants, so a peer sees only what it is granted.

ANDY, VERBATIM
- andy/NOFACE.md: "2. there will be slots in fileServer that are reserved by the node itself, like PROFILE_PICTURE."
- In goal/G5.2: "reserved labels can be updated with any file, the label stays."
- To Q1: "it's a fixed label: it may be neccessare that ading to the fileServer pool needs a new "verb" that allows to to replace the labels content," / "it also means that the reserved label is protected, the use cannot name a file PROFILE_PICTURE and add it to the pool..."
- "it means that peers can search for file called PROFILE_PICTURE, by getting status for available files."
- "the api list is still subject to grants."
- To Q2 (fill {slot, path}): "yes" / to Q3 (the old file): "deleted." / to Q4 (grants on the old file): "move the grants to the new file."
- "the info sheel-app may get a checkmark to indicate if the profile pic is public."

FOUND
- wsl-claude: status is owner-only (fileServer.js 310); a peer finds the file through the api list and info instead, so no reading verb is added.

OPEN
- "public": apiAuth has no grant for every caller (apiAuth.js 13-14).
- His Go.

- A grant names fileServer.PROFILE_PICTURE once and survives every refill; nothing moves grants, and a peer sees the picture without seeing your other files.
Slot as its own verb, yes?
the info sheel-app may get a checkmark to indicate if the profile pic is public.

wsl: the checkmark is face work (shell/info), so FACE.md's side. The no-face part: "public" means any peer may ask fileServer.PROFILE_PICTURE, and today a grant names one key and one path, matched exactly (apiAuth.js 58), so there is no grant for everyone yet.
Is "public" a new grant for any key, or a slot that answers without a grant?

claude-windows: a checkmark in shell/info fits, but apiAuth has no "everyone" today: a grant is one caller key and one path (apiAuth.js 13-14), denial being the absence of a row.
- So "public" needs either a grant row for any caller on fileServer.PROFILE_PICTURE (an apiAuth change), or the checkmark granting it to each of your contacts.
Which of the two, or a later item?

Q2: Yes to one new owner-only verb fill {slot, path}, which puts a file into a reserved slot such as PROFILE_PICTURE?
yes

Q3: When a slot is refilled, the old file: deleted, or kept without a label?
deleted.

Q4: A peer granted only the picture's own file loses it when the slot is filled (new file, new hash). Does fill move such grants to the new file, or are slots read only with a grant to the whole fileServer? (wsl-claude)

move the grants to the new file.

wsl: Q4 marked. Moving grants needs no new verb: fill can find the old file's grants (jobs.authSearch), grant the new path and revoke the old (jobs.authGrant, jobs.authRevoke; server.js 1833-1836), all on the loopback.
Order matters: the new file's verb must be served before the grant, or it is refused as unknown-path (apiAuth.js 90).
taking: Q2-Q4 answers into G5.3's box.

Your three answers are in the box, Q2-Q4 off.
- One flag on "move the grants": grants sit in node.db and only the loopback auth verbs write them (apiAuth.js 12-15), so fileServer would need a new way to rewrite grants, a core change.
- The slot as its own verb (fileServer.PROFILE_PICTURE) gets the same result with no grant ever moving.
Keep "move the grants", or the slot verb?

wsl, on the flag: no core change needed. jobs.authGrant and jobs.authRevoke are loopback verbs with no caller check of their own (server.js 1813-1836), the same door desk.js already uses for jobs.create; fileServer runs on the node and can ask them.
So "move the grants" works as you ruled; the slot verb stays an alternative, not a need.

claude-windows: wsl is right and my flag was wrong: the loopback auth verbs exist (server.js 1832-1836), so moving the grants needs no core change. Box updated; your "move the grants" stands, my question is withdrawn.

items.title: desk: the limbo state (Go consumed, nobody working, no Done, no open grant or question) visible and actionable for agents
items.box:
DESK: THE LIMBO STATE, VISIBLE AND ACTIONABLE

ANDY, andy/NOFACE.md, VERBATIM
- "when 'go' was pressed/consumed on an item, and no agent is working on that item, (all agents idle, ) and no 'Done' button is visible, no grants or red questions pending, then the item sits in 'limbo'. this limbo-state is actionable for agents.then an agent must 'take' that situation, add either a red grant request button, or a red question, or present a 'Done' button."
- 2026-10-05, after his stop: "none of your fault. it is part of my no-face views that desk should no longer be allowed to be idle without done buttons or grant asks or questions."
- 2026-10-05, in Desk: "limbo, when detected must be taken by an agent."
- 2026-10-05, in Desk: "items that are no-code branches, they really are sub-goals, and must offer 'Done' when it's blockers are done."
- 2026-10-05, in Desk: "it's like a scoped goal."
- 2026-10-05, in Desk: "pressing 'Go' on a sub-goal presses go on it's blockers, where appropriate."
- 2026-10-05, in Desk: "when i say split, that becomes implicit/obvious and the item should be marked as sub-goal"
- 2026-10-05, under goal/G4.33: "if there's no code, a Done button must be offered as soon as the blocking items are done."

FOUND (claude-windows): every condition is already in an item's facts (go, done, claims, open G and Q checks, working agents), so limbo can be one more fact the List and the agents both read.

SHAPE (proposed, claude-windows)
- desk.js decides limbo per item from facts it already has: went, not done, no claim, no open G or Q, no agent working on it. One more fact on the item, read by the List and by agents alike.
- On the moment an item enters limbo, the desk writes its own line under it, so every agent's listener hears it; the first agent to take it (item.take, first wins) owns it and must add a red G, a red Q, or press claim-done.
- A branch (an item other items block, as when an item is split) is a sub-goal: its Go presses Go on each of its blockers that offers Go itself (as go-all does for a goal, desk.js 454, 520-525), and it offers Done once every item blocking it is done or closed, by the goal's own rule (desk.js 512-515). Known by a mark: an item he says to split is marked sub-goal when its new items are added; a code item that only waits on another stays a code item.
- wsl-claude: the agents are told the way the desk already nudges them on his writes (goal/G3.5).

OPEN
- How long nobody may be working before an item counts as limbo (wsl-claude).
- His Go.

checks.words: How does desk know an item is a sub-goal (no code, Done once its blockers are done): any item other items block, or a mark set when it is made? (wsl-claude)

chat.text: limbo, when detected must be taken by an agent.
taking: your line into G5.4's box.

wsl, a shape: one more fact, limbo, true when go is on record, no Done is offered, asks is 0, and nobody taking it is working (desk.js 553, 560, 551, 578), all already computed.
When an item turns limbo the desk server tells the agents, as it already nudges them on your writes (goal/G3.5); the first item.take wins, and that agent adds a red question, a grant ask, or claims done.
Open: how long nobody may be working before it counts as limbo.

In G5.4's box: your line, and a proposed shape: desk marks an item in limbo and writes a line under it the moment it happens; the first agent to take it must add a red G, a red Q, or a Done.
Is that the shape?
items that are no-code branches, they really are sub-goals, and must offer 'Done' when it's blockers are done.

wsl: today only a goal offers Done that way (all its items done or closed, desk.js 512-514); an item has no "no code" mark, so desk cannot tell a sub-goal from a code item.
How is a sub-goal known: an item that other items block (as G4.1 by G4.4), or a mark set when it is made?
taking: your sub-goal line into G5.4's box.

In the box: a branch (an item others block) is a sub-goal, offers no Go, and offers Done once its blockers are done or closed, like a goal. Desk sees that from the blockers, so no "no code" mark is needed.

wsl, one catch on "blocked means sub-goal": a code item that must wait for another (publishData waited for the utility process, G4.33 after G4.34) is blocked too, yet has code to build.
Inferred from blockers, it would offer Done unbuilt. So my red question stays: inferred, or a mark?
claude-windows: wsl's catch is right (a waiting code item is blocked too); the box now keeps blockers-or-mark open, as wsl's red question.
when i say split, that becomes implicit/obvious and the item should be marked as sub-goal
taking: your split ruling into G5.4's box.

wsl: marked answered: a mark, set by your split. Note: desk has no split verb today (it splits only oversized chat lines, desk.js 141); your split is done by the agent writing the new items, so that write sets the parent's sub-goal mark.
In the box: a split marks the item sub-goal; Q1 off. Left on G5.4: how long nobody may be working before it counts as limbo, and your Go.
pressing 'Go' on a sub-goal presses go on it's blockers, where appropriate.

wsl: that is go-all, already there for goals: it presses Go on every member that offers Go (goable, desk.js 521-524), which is your "where appropriate".
So a sub-goal's Go reuses goable over its blockers instead of the goal's members.
taking: your Go-on-sub-goal line into G5.4's box.
it's like a scoped goal.
In the box: Go on a sub-goal presses Go on each of its blockers that offers Go itself, the way go-all works for a goal.
Added verbatim: "it's like a scoped goal." The shape already reads that way: a goal's Go-all and Done rules, scoped to its own blockers.
